reason: The wheels need drives before the rover can move, so I’ll assemble those first.
expectation: The wheels will attach to the gearmotors as a drive assembly, though it may still need fitting to the deck.

alternatives.reason: The remote also needs power, but I want to start with the moving parts.

effect: The wheel drives are assembled, and the gearboxes trade speed for greater turning force. They are ready to fit to the deck.
reaction: The speed-and-force tradeoff is a useful detail.
reason: I’ll fit the assembled drives to the rover deck to give it powered wheels.
expectation: The wheel drives will occupy the deck’s wheel-drive slot; the rover will still need its other components.

effect: The drives are fitted, and I now understand that independent wheel speeds will steer the rover without a steering axle.
reaction: That steering arrangement is interesting and straightforward.
reason: The ball caster will provide the third support point for the deck.
expectation: The caster will fit into its slot, supporting the rover while swivelling freely.

effect: The caster is fitted, completing the rover’s three support points.
reason: I’ll fit the receiver and motor driver so the remote can eventually control the wheels.
expectation: The receiver and driver will occupy their deck slot; power and switching will still need fitting.

effect: The receiver and motor driver are fitted; the deck still needs its power and switch components.
reason: I’ll fit the switch harness so the rover can be powered on and off.
expectation: The harness will fill its deck slot, with the switch kept off until assembly is ready.

effect: The switch harness is fitted; the rover battery is the remaining listed deck component.
reason: I’ll fit the battery pack to complete the deck’s listed components.
expectation: The battery pack will fit its slot, with the switch kept off until the assembly is ready.

alternatives.reason: The remote also needs batteries, but I’ll finish fitting the deck first.

effect: The battery pack is fitted, completing the listed deck slots; the gear guards are now available to install.
reaction: The fitting was predictable, but the guards feel like useful progress toward a safe test.
reason: I’ll fit the gear guards before powering or testing the rover.
expectation: The guards will cover the drive mechanisms; the remote will probably still need batteries before a test.

alternatives.reason: The remote needs power too, but I prefer to guard the moving parts first.

effect: The wiring and gear covers are in place, and the rover is ready for a remote test with its wheels clear.
reaction: The powered-off wiring and test stops make the preparation feel thoughtful.
reason: The only offered combination powers the remote, which the rover needs for testing.
expectation: The batteries will fit into the remote, making it ready to control the rover.

effect: The remote now has power and is ready to test with the guarded rover.
reason: The only offered action tests the remote against the rover.
expectation: The remote should make the raised drive wheels respond, though they may need adjustment.

effect: The raised-wheel test confirmed that the remote controls the rover’s drives, completing the chapter goal; the pen remains for later.
reaction: Seeing the steering idea tested was satisfying, though the test was brief.

mostWorthwhile.text: Fitting the drives was most worthwhile because it explained how independent wheel speeds steer without a steering axle.

leastWorthwhile.text: The separate receiver and switch fittings felt repetitive, with little to learn from their individual results.

surprise.text: I had not expected the rover to turn by varying wheel speeds rather than using a steering axle.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless, though several electrical fittings were predictable assembly steps rather than meaningful choices.

continue.text: I would continue to see the rover draw and deliver invitations; the tested drive makes that next application intriguing.
